transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-12-28 16:00 PST
- Duration: ~46 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Sam Park (CTO, Lightfield), Elena Ruiz (Lead ML Eng), Jordan Blake (Platform Eng), Nora Kim (Product)

Summary: Quick discovery focused on Lightfield's desire to get from PoC to first token quickly via self-serve, but with clear guardrails for data residency and SOC2 audit later. Discussed hosted free credits, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated customers.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, i'm maya with redwood set a quick agenda, want to understand current stack, constraints, and what success looks like for your first 90 days
[00:12] Sam (Lightfield): yeah thanks, appreciate it. we run a small inference infra and most of the dev team's protos are on AWS. we want to ship a chat-like summarization feature in Q1, but the legal team is picky about residency and audit logs so that could push us to dedicated or private for prod
[00:28] Diego (Redwood SE): totally. quick Q: for the initial rollout do you need PII redaction or full tenancy isolation?
[00:34] Elena (Lightfield): initially it's just in-product summaries of internal docs, so PII is unlikely, but the data set includes customer emails and contract text — legal wants to keep options open.
[00:43] Jordan (Platform): and two practical constraints: 1) latency target is <= 350ms p95 for short prompts, 2) cost target is under $X per 1k tokens, we have a rough budget.
[00:55] Maya: great, that's helpful. our hosted API is the fastest path — free credits to experiment, SDKs, and time-to-first-token under an hour typically. Dedicated gives predictability and isolation; Private gives you full control and can be deployed into your VPC or on-prem for audits
[01:10] Sam: can you run a quick example of time-to-first-token? like, how fast can we get devs calling the API with a sample prompt set?
[01:18] Maya: yes we can get you started today. i'll share the quickstart link and a token bundle. typical flow is sign up, create an API key, run the example repo — many teams hit first token in 20-60 minutes.
[01:29] Elena: and for the dedicated pilot, do you require long-term commitments?
[01:33] Diego: for Dedicated we do reserved capacity with monthly or annual commits, but we have pilot programs — a short trial with burst capacity to validate throughput. basically you can test workload patterns before committing
[01:45] Nora (Product): curious about observability — we need per-route latency and cost breakdowns for product analytics.
[01:51] Diego: Redwood Console gives per-model and per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, and tracing hooks. we'll also attach request metadata so you can map product flows to spend
[02:05] Jordan: what about caching? our usage pattern has lots of repeated prefixes in chat, could that drive price down?
[02:11] Maya: yes automatic prefix and KV caching can reduce per-token cost; we'll help configure a batching and cache profile as part of the pilot
[02:18] Sam: security question: do you have SOC2 and encryption key management? legal will want to see integrations with our KMS or HSM
[02:25] Diego: we have SOC2 reports and support KMS integrations for Private and Dedicated; hosted also supports customer-managed keys for enterprise tiers. i'll share the security pack after the call
[02:36] Elena: any gotchas with network egress or VPC peering? our infra team is strict about egress audit logs
[02:41] Diego: for Private we can do VPC peering and customer-managed networking, Dedicated can be isolated to a VPC, hosted obviously routes through our network but we provide audit logs and VPC-style controls for enterprise customers
[02:55] Sam: what about model variants and fallbacks? we want graceful degradation if a larger model is busy
[03:02] Diego: smart routing supports fallbacks by policy — route by latency, cost, or region. we can pin model versions and set automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants to hit SLOs
[03:15] Maya: quick note on pricing: i'll send the hosted per-token and embedding rates and a Dedicated pilot pricing sheet. we can include an estimate for typical conversational traffic once you share prompt set and 24h volumes
[03:26] Nora: how do you handle RBAC and SSO for Console?
[03:29] Diego: we support SAML/SSO, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access controls. audit logs are available with retention options for enterprise add-ons
[03:40] Jordan: do you support on-prem for air-gapped environments? we have a customer that might require that later
[03:44] Diego: yes Private can be packaged for on-prem air-gapped installs; those are enterprise engagements but feasible
[03:50] Sam: excellent. can we talk about success criteria for the pilot — what would make us move from hosted trial to dedicated?
[03:56] Maya: success criteria we typically recommend: 1) performance: meet p95 latency targets under representative load; 2) cost: demonstrate acceptable per-token unit economics after batching/caching; 3) security/compliance: SOC2 + KMS/SSO checkboxes validated; 4) dev experience: time-to-first-token for other engineers < 1 day
[04:17] Elena: that's good. on the perf point, our current infra yields ~280ms p95 for local models, so we want comparable latency with the hosted path
[04:26] Diego: for short prompts we can show sub-300ms p95 on certain instance types; i'll propose a benchmark plan to replicate your workload
[04:34] Sam: what do you need from us to set up the benchmark?
[04:36] Diego: sample prompt set, 24h traffic shape, target SLOs, and any privacy constraints. we'll spin up a dedicated pilot instance or use hosted with pinning to mimic the production config
[04:48] Nora: any risks we should flag to execs?
[04:50] Maya: early risk is underestimating token churn — we can mitigate with caching and prompt engineering. another is data residency — that's why Private is on the table for later stages
[04:58] Sam: earlier you mentioned free credits — how are those applied?
[05:02] Maya: we issue a credits bundle tied to your account that applies to hosted usage. they expire in 90 days typically. for Dedicated pilots we can convert some credit to discounted pilot hours
[05:12] Elena: is there a self-serve UI to create keys for devs? or do you have to go through an AE?
[05:16] Maya: self-serve account creation and key generation is available; for enterprise features we sometimes enable via a support ticket. most devs won't need us to create keys
[05:26] Jordan: constraints: we run strict egress monitoring and have to keep logs for 12 months for audits; can you store request-level logs for that period?
[05:33] Diego: yes, audit log retention is configurable for enterprise tiers; we can export logs to your S3 or SIEM too
[05:40] Sam: any performance impact when customer-managed keys are used?
[05:44] Diego: negligible for normal tokens; some HSM flows add minor latency at key exchange time but runtime inference isn't materially affected
[05:52] Nora: what's the typical SLA for Dedicated? uptime + latency targets?
[05:56] Diego: Dedicated gets SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll include specifics in the pilot SLA doc. hosted has best-effort but high reliability for PLG users
[06:07] Maya: ok next practical step: we'll send the quickstart link and a hosted credits bundle today, diego will draft a benchmark plan and security pack, and sam will share prompts and traffic shape
[06:18] Sam: sounds good. can we schedule the benchmark session for next week?
[06:21] Maya: yes propose Wed 2026-01-08 or Thu 01-09, i'll send a doodle and lock it in
[06:28] Elena: one small question — do you support streaming responses and function calls now?
[06:33] Diego: yes streaming is supported and we have function/tool calling primitives; small caveat some older model variants don't support structured tool output but most curated open models do
[06:45] Jordan: competitor question, do you have advantages vs Anthropic for production ops?
[06:48] Maya: we emphasize production-grade runtime, smart routing, and developer experience — the main differentiation is the unified control plane across hosted, Dedicated, and Private and tooling for cost controls
[06:56] Sam: ok great. any final Qs?
[06:58] Nora: just one — will you share a short pilot MOU for internal review?
[07:02] Maya: yes we'll attach a pilot MOU with the pricing sheet, nothing long — standard terms to cover pilot capacity and NDAs if needed
[07:10] Diego: i'll also include a checklist for infra (ports, IP allowlist, egress requirements) so your platform team can prep
[07:17] Sam: thanks everyone, appreciated the clarity. looking forward to the quickstart and benchmark
[07:20] Maya: thanks all — we'll follow up with materials and calendar invites
